File No.................... Date May 22nd, 1942.
SUBJECT: Membership and Activities of the "Independent Australia League" in Shanghai.

Further to report dated May 21, 1942, submitted by this Section, on the subject of the formation of the "Independent Australia League" enquiries go to show that Mrs. J.V. Everett, the Secretary of the Social Section, is no longer connected with the League in that capacity and is reported to have applied for repatriation. Mr. Alan W. Raymond has now taken over what was formerly known as the offices of the Social Section at Room 522 Hamilton House, however, the functions of the office in connection with the assistance to indigent foreigners have ceased.

The Breakaway Australia Movement contrary to expectations has not progressed from its embryo state as no further meetings with a view of pushing the programme forward were held. Mr. A.W. Raymond's activities in connection with the movement are somewhat confined to writing articles which appear in the daily edition of the Evening Post & Mercury.

Continued observation of the contents of the articles show that they are written in a more moderate terms with reference to the "Breakaway Australia Movement" and that they now deal chiefly with political events covering a wide field including war operations plus comments on the existing situation.

主题：上海“澳大利亚独立联盟”的成员构成及活动情况。

继本股于1942年5月21日提交的关于成立“澳大利亚独立联盟”的报告之后，经查询得知，社交股秘书 J.V. Everett 夫人已不再以该身份参与联盟事务，据报已申请遣返。Alan W. Raymond 先生现已接管原位于汉密尔顿大楼522室的社交股办公室，然而，该办公室协助贫困外国人的职能已停止。

出乎意料的是，“澳大利亚分离运动”并未脱离其萌芽状态，因为未再举行旨在推进该计划的会议。A.W. Raymond 先生与该运动相关的活动 somewhat 局限于为《晚邮报与水星报》（Evening Post & Mercury）日报版撰写文章。

持续观察文章内容显示，这些文章在提及“澳大利亚分离运动”时措辞更为温和，目前主要涉及涵盖广泛领域的政治事件，包括战争行动以及对当前局势的评论。

SUBJECT: Membership and Activities of the
"Independent Australia League" in
Shanghai

* See N/163(C)

With reference to the newly-formed
"Independent Australia League" in Shanghai, inaugurated
as the result of a "Breakaway Australia" movement
promoted by Mr. Alan W. Raymond, discreet enquiries
made among the local Australian community as well as
information obtained from those closely connected
with the promoters of the movement show that the
activities of the League subsequent to the meetings
held at the Palace Hotel, at Room 101, are confined
to what appears to be social meetings among a limited
number of supporters.

Following the announcement which appeared
in the local foreign press to the effect that messages
will be transmitted to Australia by Mr. Roy Stewart
of Radio Station XNHA, the majority of the local
Australians as well as other nationals availed
themselves of this opportunity to send messages to
their relatives and friends. Among them several, it
is reported, communicated with the League for purely
selfish purposes in as much as they were able to get
in touch with people in Australia.

It should be mentioned that although a
considerable section of the local Australian community
is now a part of the Organization, there are few who
owing to the political aspect of the body are willing
to come forward and announce their names as that of
supporters of the movement. There is little doubt
that the Organization's ideas of an independent

主题：上海“澳大利亚独立联盟”的成员构成及活动情况

* 参见 N/163(C)

关于上海新成立的“澳大利亚独立联盟”，该联盟是 Alan W. Raymond 先生推动的“澳大利亚分离运动”的结果，经向当地澳大利亚社群进行谨慎查询，并从与运动发起者关系密切的人士处获得的信息显示，在 Palace Hotel（华懋饭店）101室举行会议后，该联盟的活动仅限于似乎是在有限数量的支持者之间进行的社交聚会。

继本地外文报刊刊登公告称 XNHA 电台的 Roy Stewart 先生将向澳大利亚传送消息后，大多数本地澳大利亚人以及其他国籍人士利用此机会向亲友发送消息。据报，其中有几人纯粹出于自私目的与联盟联系，因为他们能够借此与澳大利亚的人取得联系。

值得一提的是，虽然当地澳大利亚社群中有相当一部分人现在是该组织的一部分，但由于该团体的政治性质，很少有人愿意站出来宣布自己是该运动的支持者。毫无疑问，该组织关于独立的

The functions of the Social Section elected for the purpose of raising funds for relief of needy Australians in Shanghai, up to the present, were on a very limited scale. Occasional observation of the offices of the Social Section which are located at Room 522, Hamilton House, shows that Mrs. J.V. Everett, the Honorary Social Secretary, is seldom in attendance and that no applicants have so far appeared for assistance.
During a visit to the above mentioned offices it was learnt that Mrs. J.V. Everett does not reside there and that the three roomed apartment with the exception of one room which serves as the reception office, is empty.
The Active Committee of the "Independent Australia League" is now consisting of the following members :-
1. Mr. Alan W. Raymond - the Head of the Organization.
2. Mrs. J.V. Everett - the Secretary of the Social Section.
3. Mr. J.J. Holland - member of the Committee.
4. Miss Joan MacDonald - XMHA Australia programme. broadcaster
5. Mr. Roy Stewart - in charge of the XMHA Australia programme.

在访问上述办公室期间获悉，J.V. Everett 夫人并不居住在此，除了一间用作接待办公室的房间外，这套三居室的公寓是空的。

Enquiries ascertained that among others,
the following prominent members of the local Australian
community attended the meetings at the Palace Hotel:-

Mrs. Taylor - Principal of the "Peter

Mrs. Ambrose.

Mr. H. Cumming - an Architect.

Mrs. Cook.

Mr. R.G. Woodhead - of the Shanghai
Power Company.

Mr. Coleman - of the Jardine Matheson
Co.

The last two persons mentioned are known
as staunch British patriots and their appearance at
one of the meetings was unexpected.

Alan Willoughby Raymond, a broker by
profession; born in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia,
32 years ago, speaks fluent Cantonese dialect and
for the most part of his residence in China associated
with Chinese socially as well as on business matters.
He first came to Shanghai in 1928 and for the following
eleven years is reported to have been engaged in the
marble business, was employed as a salesman, correspon-
dent, import and export business and finally as an
exchange broker. He is an ardent horse racing follower
and through his association with the Race Club and
lavish expenditure of money accumulated a number of
debts which practically ruined his business.

Following the outbreak of the Sino-
Japanese Hostilities in 1937, he proceeded to Wusih
to take charge of a Chinese factory there. With the

Following his return to Shanghai, A.W.
Raymond was engaged in several business ventures
but has always suffered from lack of capital. He is
now engaged in an import and export business and is
the manager of the "Asiatic Commercial Corporation"
located at Suite 304, 299 Szechuen Road.

A.W. Raymond is a capable journalist and
has displayed some organizing ability when he embarked
upon the Breakaway Australia movement. He is now
writing interesting articles under the heading of "An
Aussie's Point of View" which appear in the daily
edition of the Evening Post/Mercury.

Mrs. Jacqueline Valerie Everett, Australian
born journalist, is reported to have travelled widely;
having lived in many parts of Europe and America. Little
is known of her activities outside of being an active
member of the "Breakaway Australia Movement". The fact
that she is a qualified nurse indicates that she has
had medical training and her pleasant and capable
personality confirms reports that she is socially
well accepted. However, there are rumours that her
undertaking of the post of the Honorary Social Secretary
is purely for publicity purposes; since there are very
few indigent Australians in Shanghai who as a rule
are assisted by the Salvation Army Hostel located at
6 Yang Terrace.

Jacqueline Valerie Everett 夫人，出生于澳大利亚的记者，据报游历广泛；曾在欧洲和美国的许多地方生活过。除了作为“澳大利亚分离运动”的活跃成员外，人们对她的活动知之甚少。她是一名合格护士的事实表明她受过医疗培训，而她令人愉快且能干的个性证实了她在社交界广受接受的报道。然而，有谣言称她担任荣誉社交秘书一职纯粹是为了宣传目的；因为上海贫困的澳大利亚人很少，这些人通常由位于杨氏露台6号的救世军招待所提供援助。

John Joseph Holland, an Australian, 34
years old, now in the employ of German Radio Station,
X.G.R.S., has been a close associate of A.W. Raymond
throughout their travels in the Far East/

He first came to this city from Hongkong in
1937 and was making a living as a free-lance journalist
writing stories for local correspondents of foreign
newspapers. Prior to his arrival here, he was connected
with the "Hongkong Daily Press" where he obtained
casual employment with the assistance of one Frank
Cade, an Australian editor who was financially support-
ing him and A.W. Raymond when they arrived in the city
in straitened circumstances. J.J. Holland is known to
have unsuccessfully applied for enlistment in the
Hongkong Police. In 1938, he is reported to have
visited Singapore where he acquired some wealth working
in a mining concern and in fact contemplated to open a
mining company in partnership with one named Patterson.
He first came to the notice of S.M. Police in 1939
when the Passport Officer of H.B.M.Consulate in Shanghai
asked Police assistance in locating Mr. J.J. Holland
following a receipt of communication from the Hongkong
Government to the effect that a Maintenance Order had
been issued against him in Australia on the complaint of
his wife Emily Muriel Holland. According to Police
reports, J.J. Holland in 1941 was acting on behalf of
General "One Arm" Sutton in Shanghai and was negotiating
to import firearms. He was in possession of a letter
stating that he was General Sutton's representative
and is believed to have approached officials of the

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

An
Aussie's
Point
Of View

BY ALAN RAYMOND
AUSTRALIA'S Special Envoy to America, Dr. H. V. Evatt, yesterday spent four hours conferring with President Roosevelt and Mr. Harry Hopkins. On conclusion of the conference, Dr. Evatt declined to tell newsmen anything regarding the matters discussed but intimated that he expected to have another talk with the President again next week. Mr. Casey and two other members of the Australian mission although presented to the President, did not take part in the long discussion. Evidently, Mr. Casey, in view of his reprehensible conduct no longer enjoys the confidence of the Australian Government and beyond winding up his affairs, is not to participate in the intimate negotiations now being carried on. Mr. Casey is, to all intents and purposes, now in the British camp and so the less he has to do with Australian affairs the better for Australia.

Lord Strabolgi, speaking on the occasion of the opening of "Warship Week" at London, illuminated the strategic importance of Ceylon, when he said: "He who has Ceylon dominates the most important sea route of the world." "Ceylon with its fortified naval base in Trincomalee is of even greater importance to the Allies than Malaya or Singapore. The loss of Ceylon would enable the Japanese to stretch out their hand to the Germans in the Middle East which would be a great catastrophe for us." In concluding, he demanded that "Sir Stafford Cripps should pay a visit to Ceylon after having completed his mission in India in order to see to it that all the measures necessary for the defense of the island be carried out."

Lord Strabolgi's reference to Ceylon spotlights the island as one of the next most likely points of Japanese attention. Heretofore, Singapore was always declared to be the greatest and most important base of the Allies in Eastern waters. Now that Singapore is gone, it is probably true that Ceylon assumes the position of most important British base. Lord Strabolgi, being a naval expert of the old school ignores the fact that fixed fortifications have proved themselves almost valueless in the mobility of the attacking forces and their ability to outflank them, thereby neutralising any value they were thought to have possessed. Moreover, from the point of view of geographical position, Singapore cannot be compared with Ceylon. Singapore commands the Pacific or Indian Oceans, the entrance of which can only be outflanked by sea by a long detour of many thousands of miles through the Pacific which, at that period, was held and patrolled by enemy forces. Ceylon, however, is placed about midway between Singapore and the African Continent entirely surrounded by the open waters of the Indian Ocean, affording great freedom of action for manoeuvre to attacking enemy naval forces.

AUSTRALIA has practically given up all hope of reinforcement from any other quarter but the United States and although this is indeed a slim hope, Australia's attention is now turned almost exclusively to the Pacific. By following a circuitous detour around the southern Pacific, it is just possible that American ships may reach south-eastern Australia. However with the steady extension of Japanese activities through the islands off the north-east of Australia and the naval patrol of all sea lanes to Australia the chance of American ships being able to make Australian ports is very slight.

It is interesting to note the Allied opinion, as expressed by a number of military experts that the Japanese would not attempt to make a landing at Darwin owing to the arid nature of the hinterland and the vast distance across waterless country to the populated districts of the east and south-east. However such a possibility cannot be entirely ruled out. The longest way round is sometimes the shortest way there, as the Japanese demonstrated in Malaya and elsewhere. There is a railway line running from Darwin through central Australia, to the south, and although in the event of an Australian retreat southward, the line would no doubt be destroyed in part, Japanese engineers have proved themselves capable of repairing and utilizing such facilities with surprising speed. In mountainous country or jungle, mechanised forces are limited in speed by conditions. The same does not apply to the central Australian plains. Most of the country in inland Australia is first one vast plain. Ideal country for the fast movement of mechanised forces and natural landing fields abound. Providing the Japanese forces can muster sufficient supplies and vehicles to successfully solve the problem of supply, why shouldn't they attempt an overland invasion through the heart of Australia? Mechanized forces could cover in many sections 200 miles a day, whilst defence would be quite negligible in this territory. A glance at the map will show the enormous advantages to be gained by the Japanese, should they adopt this plan of attack. In the event of them doing so, they would naturally make simultaneous attacks from the sea at various points around the coast. A review of the situation reveals that the possibility of an overland campaign through Darwin and central Australia is not an impossibility after all but quite feasible. The ingenuity of the Japanese forces in adapting their methods of warfare to overcome hitherto insurmountable obstacles has become only too well known to the Allies, and the possibility of such a strategy being used should not be lightly overlooked.

一个
澳洲人的
观点

作者：ALAN RAYMOND
澳大利亚驻美特使 H. V. Evatt 博士昨日花费四小时与罗斯福总统及 Harry Hopkins 先生举行会谈。会谈结束后，Evatt 博士拒绝向新闻记者透露任何关于讨论事项的内容，但暗示他预计下周将再次与总统交谈。Casey 先生及澳大利亚代表团的其他两名成员虽被引见给总统，但未参与长时间的讨论。显然，鉴于 Casey 先生应受谴责的行为，他已不再享有澳大利亚政府的信任，除了处理收尾事务外，他将不参与目前正在进行的机密谈判。Casey 先生实际上现已处于英国阵营，因此他越少介入澳大利亚事务，对澳大利亚越有利。

Strabolgi 勋爵在伦敦“战舰周”开幕式上发表讲话时，阐明了锡兰的战略重要性，他说：“谁拥有锡兰，谁就掌控了世界上最重要的海上航线。”“锡兰及其在亭可马里设防的海军基地，对盟国而言甚至比马来亚或新加坡更为重要。失去锡兰将使日本人能够向中东的德国人伸出援手，这对我们将是一场巨大的灾难。”最后，他要求“斯塔福德·克里普斯爵士（Sir Stafford Cripps）在完成印度使命后访问锡兰，以确保执行保卫该岛所需的一切措施。”

Strabolgi 勋爵对锡兰的提及，突显了该岛作为日本下一个最可能的关注点之一。此前，新加坡一直被称为盟国在东方水域最大和最重要的基地。既然新加坡已经失守，锡兰取代其成为最重要的英国基地的说法可能是真的。Strabolgi 勋爵作为旧派海军专家，忽视了固定堡垒在进攻部队的机动性及其迂回包抄能力面前已被证明几乎毫无价值，从而中和了其被认为拥有的任何价值这一事实。此外，从地理位置来看，新加坡无法与锡兰相提并论。新加坡扼守太平洋或印度洋的入口，若要从海上迂回包抄，需经由太平洋绕行数千英里，而当时太平洋由敌军控制并巡逻。然而，锡兰位于新加坡与非洲大陆之间的大致中间位置，完全被印度洋的开阔水域包围，为敌方海军进攻部队提供了极大的机动自由。

澳大利亚实际上已放弃除美国以外任何其他地方增援的希望，尽管这希望确实渺茫，但澳大利亚的注意力现在几乎完全转向太平洋。通过绕道南太平洋的曲折路线，美国船只有可能抵达澳大利亚东南部。然而，随着日本活动在澳大利亚东北部岛屿间的稳步扩展，以及对所有通往澳大利亚的海上航线的海军巡逻，美国船只能够抵达澳大利亚港口的机会非常渺茫。

值得注意的是，许多军事专家表达的盟国观点认为，由于腹地干旱以及跨越无水地区到达东部和东南部人口稠密区的距离遥远，日本不会尝试在达尔文登陆。然而，这种可能性不能完全排除。有时最远的路反而是最近的路，正如日本人在马来亚和其他地方所演示的那样。有一条铁路线从达尔文穿过澳大利亚中部向南延伸，虽然如果澳大利亚向南撤退，该线路无疑会被部分破坏，但日本工程师已证明他们能够以惊人的速度修复并利用此类设施。在山区或丛林中，机械化部队的速度受条件限制。但这并不适用于澳大利亚中部平原。澳大利亚内陆大部分地区首先是一片广阔的平原。这是机械化部队快速移动的理想地形，且天然着陆场 abound（众多）。只要日本军队能集结足够的物资和车辆以成功解决补给问题，他们为何不尝试穿越澳大利亚腹地的陆上入侵呢？机械化部队在许多路段每天可覆盖 200 英里，而该地区的防御几乎可以忽略不计。看一眼地图就会发现，如果日本人采取这种攻击计划，他们将获得巨大的优势。如果他们这样做，他们自然会在沿海各处同时发动海上攻击。回顾局势表明，通过达尔文和澳大利亚中部进行陆战的可能性并非不可能，而是相当可行的。日本军队调整作战方法以克服此前不可逾越的障碍的独创性已为盟国所熟知，不应轻视使用此种策略的可能性。

19 MAR. 1942

An
Aussie's
Point
Of View

BY ALAN RAYMOND

REITERATING Premier Tojo's fair warning to the Australian people, Mr. Tomokazu Hori in Tokyo yesterday said: "Every indication shows that Australia is going to follow the fate of the Netherlands East Indies." Quoting press despatches Mr. Hori pointed out that the Australian War Minister Mr. Francis Forde has been instructed to attack Japanese force. He added however that the information does not disclose who issued such an order or where they are to attack Japanese forces" regretfully added. "If it is so, it is a pity for all the Australian people."

I have only to echo Mr. Hori's regrets that Australia has so far failed to avail herself of the Japanese Government's offers to discuss terms. It is inconceivable how under present circumstances the Australian Government can continue their blind policy of resistance which will surely bring sorrow and disaster to the Australian people. It is not the time to doubt the sincerity of the Japanese Government's intentions. There is no choice which would admit of such thoughts. Australia is confronted today with the inescapable fact that she faces national extinction if she continues in the same policy which has already brought her to the present impasse. No one in the world doubts the courage and bravery of the Australian people but there is no connection between such qualities and cowardly madness.

Apart from military force issues, with which Australia is faced today, we must also consider whether the present conflict with Japan is based entirely on sound logical reasons. A state of being could be maintained indefinitely unless it is logical and natural. Australia's inclusion in the European bloc both economically and politically was certainly neither Australia is undoubtedly a complement of Asia and fits into the Asiatic and Western Pacific scheme of economics as perfectly as a piece of a jig-saw puzzle. The artificial status of Australia as a part of the European scheme could not last forever and a very interesting problem arises now as to whether a European population can be assimilated into the Asiatic scheme harmoniously. This of course depends largely on the ability of the Australian people to realize their true position and the inevitability of the evolutionary changes taking place at present. If the Australian people prove capable of adapting themselves to the changing circumstances and will co-operate sincerely in the new scheme of things then there is no reason why they should not be able to continue their natural development and be one of the leading components of the Western Pacific bloc. Australia needs for its development a large influx of people and is capable of absorbing probably ten times the number of its present population.

AUSTRALIA possesses as yet an enormous untouched natural wealth in minerals, lumber etc. as well as being the world's greatest producer of wool and many essential foodstuffs. Most people in Australia unfortunately are grossly misinformed regarding Asiatic peoples. They imagine that given a chance the Japanese will descend on them in countless hordes which will result in the complete sweeping away of their jealously-guarded standard of living. Little do they know that the Japanese people love their own country better than any other part of the world and that the Japanese Government encounters difficulty in inducing them to emigrate abroad.

Japanese land forces in New Guinea have made a surprise advance across country through the jungle to attack Port Moresby from the land when they were expected to make an attack from the sea. Their experience gained in the South East Asian jungles has made them veritable masters of what was hitherto thought impenetrable jungle. It seems that they were able to turn what were regarded as serious military obstacles into advantages for themselves. Several other fortified islands off the north east coast of Australia have also been attacked from the air as Japanese forces systematically pave the way for a full-scale invasion.

1942年3月19日

一位
澳大利亚人
的
观点

作者：艾伦·雷蒙德（Alan Raymond）

昨日在东京，堀智一（Tomokazu Hori）先生重申了东条英机首相对澳大利亚人民的公正警告，他说：“所有迹象表明，澳大利亚将步荷属东印度群岛的后尘。”堀先生援引新闻电讯指出，澳大利亚战争部长弗朗西斯·福德（Francis Forde）先生已受命攻击日军。但他补充说，该消息并未披露是谁下达了此类命令，也未说明将在何处攻击日军”，他遗憾地补充道。“如果真是如此，那对所有澳大利亚人民来说是一种悲哀。”

我只能附和堀先生对澳大利亚迄今未能利用日本政府提出的讨论条款之提议的遗憾。在目前的情况下，澳大利亚政府继续其盲目的抵抗政策，这必将给澳大利亚人民带来悲痛和灾难，这是令人难以理解的。现在不是怀疑日本政府意图诚意的时候。没有任何选择余地容许产生此类想法。澳大利亚今天面临着无法逃避的事实，即如果她继续执行已使其陷入当前僵局的同一政策，她将面临国家灭亡。世上无人怀疑澳大利亚人民的勇气和勇敢，但这些品质与懦弱的疯狂之间没有任何联系。

除了澳大利亚今天面临的军事力量问题外，我们还必须考虑目前与日本的冲突是否完全基于合理的逻辑理由。一种状态除非是合乎逻辑和自然的，否则无法无限期维持。澳大利亚在经济和政治上被纳入欧洲集团，这肯定既非……澳大利亚无疑是亚洲的补充，并像拼图的一块那样完美地契合亚洲和西太平洋的经济体系。澳大利亚作为欧洲体系一部分的人为地位不可能永远持续，现在出现了一个非常有趣的问题，即欧洲人口能否和谐地融入亚洲体系。这当然在很大程度上取决于澳大利亚人民认识其真实地位以及当前正在发生的演变变化之必然性的能力。如果澳大利亚人民证明自己能够适应变化的环境，并真诚地配合新的事物格局，那么他们没有理由不能继续其自然发展，并成为西太平洋集团的主要组成部分之一。澳大利亚的发展需要大量人口流入，并且有能力吸收可能十倍于其目前人口的数量。

澳大利亚拥有巨大的未开发天然财富，如矿产、木材等，同时也是世界上最大的羊毛和许多基本食品生产国。不幸的是，大多数澳大利亚人对亚洲民族存在严重误解。他们想象一旦有机会，日本人将成群结队地涌来，这将导致他们精心维护的生活水平被彻底扫除。他们很少知道，日本人民热爱自己的祖国胜过世界任何其他地方，而且日本政府在诱导他们移民海外方面遇到困难。

在新几内亚的日本陆军部队出乎意料地穿越丛林向陆地推进，从陆路攻击莫尔兹比港，而人们原本预计他们会从海上发动攻击。他们在东南亚丛林中获得的经验使他们成为了此前被认为不可穿透的丛林的真正主人。看来他们能够将那些被视为严重军事障碍的因素转化为自身的优势。澳大利亚东北海岸外的其他几个设防岛屿也遭到了空袭，因为日军正在系统地为一场全面入侵铺平道路。

2 MAR. 1942

SHANGHAI TIMES.

XMHA To Introduce New
Aussie Programme Daily

The Independent Australian League in Shanghai will inaugurate a short-wave radio programme to be broadcast daily from Station XMHA beginning on Monday at 9 a.m. "The Shanghai Times" learnt yesterday. This will be the official programme of the League and will be specially transmitted to Australia.

The programme will consist of special features, in keeping with the basic principles of the Independent League, and calculated to acquaint Australians in the mother country with a wider view of Far Eastern conditions. The period of transmission will require two and a half hours, and it will be on the air daily starting from 9 a.m.

Special Features
Mr. Roy Stewart will be programme chairman. The programme will include a number of special features and musical novelties which have not been broadcast before. There will be musical interludes, two special features entitled "Introducing Japan," and "From an Australia Girl in Shanghai to an Australian Girl in Australia," by Joan MacDonald, a musical whirlabout, and an interesting novelty called "Joan and Roy."

Of particular interest to Australians in Shanghai who have found it difficult to communicate with relatives in the mother country is the announcement that directly after the news period, there will be a 15-minute programme of "Letters to Australia." Short personal messages will thus be transmitted over the ether to Australia, and this service will not cost Australians in Shanghai anything.

Australia Messages
In order to avoid congestion at the XMHA premises on the day of the broadcast, it was suggested that Australians who intend to avail themselves of the free service should send their messages to Mr. Stewart, care of XMHA, a few days previous. These should be short and crisp and not over-elaborated.

The first of the daily programmes will be broadcast on Monday morning starting at 9. It will end at 11.30 a.m.

《上海泰晤士报》

XMHA电台将每日推出
新的澳大利亚节目

据《上海泰晤士报》昨日获悉，上海独立澳大利亚联盟（Independent Australian League）将于周一上午9点起，通过XMHA电台每日广播一档短波无线电节目。这将是该联盟的官方节目，并将专门向澳大利亚传输。

该节目将包含符合独立联盟基本原则的特色栏目，旨在让母国的澳大利亚人更广泛地了解远东局势。播出时长为两个半小时，每天上午9点开始播出。

特色栏目
罗伊·斯图尔特（Roy Stewart）先生将担任节目主席。节目将包括许多以前从未广播过的特色栏目和新颖音乐曲目。将有音乐插曲，两个分别题为“介绍日本”和“由上海的一位澳大利亚女孩致澳大利亚的一位澳大利亚女孩”（作者：琼·麦克唐纳 Joan MacDonald）的特色栏目，一段音乐回旋曲，以及一个名为“琼与罗伊”的有趣新颖节目。

Date 11 / 3 / 42

AUSSIE LEADER

Mr. Allen Raymond, leader of the local Australian Independence Movement, who first launched the "get away" movement of Australia from Britain in 1928 when his organization was banned by British authorities.

Local Aussie Group Leader States Policy

Pointing out that his body is not "anti-anybody" but just pro-Australian, Mr. Allen Raymond, organizer of the newly-formed Australian Independence Group in Shanghai, expressed the hope yesterday that his organization would become the nucleus of an Overseas Australian Patriots' League.

Laying stress on the possible misunderstanding of "poorly informed people" with which his organization may meet, Mr. Raymond expressed his readiness to fight against this handicap. "If is useless and profitless in the present juncture to indulge in highly involved recriminations," Mr. Raymond declared, adding that "we hope that Australia will benefit from mistakes of the past. It is with the future that we must chiefly concern ourselves."

Independence Wanted
Mr. Raymond further revealed that it is a foregone conclusion that at the end of the present conflict Australia, if she still has the necessary autonomy to choose her own political status, will elect to be entirely independent. "We would like to see a free and independent Australia today, outside the scheme of European politics," Mr. Raymond said.

The immediate object of the newly-formed body, it was said, is to convince countrymen at home of the commonsense logic of the organization's ideas. The acceptance of this idea would spare Australia the many unnecessary horrors of a hopeless war, Mr. Raymond declared.

Spontaneous Movement
This movement is an entirely spontaneous one amongst local Australians and it is hoped that Australians in the entire East will come forward to support it, Mr. Raymond said.

The next meeting of the Australian Independence Group will take place at 4 p.m. tomorrow at the Palace Hotel and hope was expressed that all native-born Australians would attend the proceedings. The message of the Independent group, Mr. Raymond revealed, will be relayed by short wave radio so as to enable all native-born Australians in the Far East to come forward in support of the newly-formed movement.

P. A. to O. i/c.

当地澳大利亚团体领导人陈述政策

上海新成立的澳大利亚独立小组组织者艾伦·雷蒙德（Allen Raymond）先生昨天表示，他的团体并非“反对任何人”，而是仅仅支持澳大利亚，他希望他的组织能成为海外澳大利亚爱国者联盟的核心。

雷蒙德先生强调其组织可能会遇到“信息灵通程度不足的人”的误解，并表示愿意克服这一障碍。雷蒙德宣称：“在当前关头，沉溺于高度复杂的相互指责是无用且无利的，”他补充说，“我们希望澳大利亚能从过去的错误中受益。我们必须主要关注未来。”

渴望独立
雷蒙德先生进一步透露，毫无疑问，在目前冲突结束时，如果澳大利亚仍拥有选择其政治地位的必要自主权，它将选择完全独立。雷蒙德先生说：“我们希望今天看到一个自由独立的澳大利亚，置身于欧洲政治体系之外。”

据说，这个新成立团体的直接目标是让国内的同胞相信该组织理念的常识性逻辑。雷蒙德先生宣称，接受这一理念将使澳大利亚免于一场无望战争带来的许多不必要的恐怖。

自发运动

SHANGHAI TIMES.
16 MAR. 1942
Activities Of
Aussie Group
Are Extended
Social Section Formed
To Raise Funds For
Needy Countrymen
With the Independent Australia League, headed by Mr. Allen Raymond, gaining greater support from the local Australian community, the organization announced yesterday the formation of a Social Section to be headed by Mrs. J. V. Everett, who was nominated Honorary Social Secretary.
A well-known member of the local Australian community, Mrs. Everett has travelled widely, having lived in many parts of Europe and America. In addition to her many other accomplishments, Mrs. Everett is a well-known journalist and a qualified nurse. Of a pleasant and capable personality, Mrs. Everett is well liked in Shanghai so that the League is indeed fortunate to have her valuable services at its disposal.
Relief Planned
Interviewed upon her assumption of duties as Honorary Social Secretary of the Independent Australia League, Mrs. Everett pointed out that her programme will be arranged so as to enable the body, from the very beginning, to raise funds for relief of local Australians in financial difficulties.
Mrs. Everett urged all local Australians desirous of lending a helping hand in this direction to communicate with her as soon as possible at her home, 522 Hamilton House, telephone 16453.
Radio Messages Sent
Meanwhile, scores of radio messages are being sent by local Australians to their countrymen at home and in other parts of East Asia through radio station XMHA. The messages, some of them of a very touching character, are aimed to bring home to Australians the urgent need to accept the generous offer made by the Japanese Government and withdraw from a pointless war thus sparing Australia all the unnecessary horrors of a war which is not their own.
All Australians desirous of sending messages to their relatives at home are advised to communicate with Mr. Roy Steward who is in charge of the short wave transmission of the messages over station XMHA.

SHANGHAI TIMES.
17 MAR. 1942

Local Australian Body To
Hold Another Meet

The Independent Australia League will convene a meeting at the Palace Hotel, Room 101 at 5 p.m. today for the election of a committee and various officers. Mr. Allen Raymond, Chairman of the body, told "The Shanghai Times" yesterday.

All Australians are asked to attend, as discussions will be held touching on different matters in connection with the League and especially with regard to the question of relief for needy Australians.

The election, Mr. Raymond stated, will be held expressly for the purpose of putting the League on a more established basis, as up till now the body is only in an organizing stage. Its policies and aims will be also crystallized during the meeting this afternoon, and permanent officers will be chosen.

Questioned with regard to the number of Australians who have already joined the League, Mr. Raymond declared that a considerable section of the local Australian community is now a part of the organization but that owing to the political aspect of the body, it is at present not desirable to mention their names.

Mrs. J. V. Everctt, nominated Honorary Social Secretary of the newly formed Social Section of the League, will be mainly concerned in the question of relief for Australians, it was stated, and any person, desirous of lending a helping hand, should communicate with her at 522 Hamilton House, telephone 16453.

Aim Of Australians

Mr. Raymond had previously asserted to the press that it was a foregone conclusion that at the termination of the present World War, Australia would elect to become entirely independent if she would be given the power to choose her own political status, it will be recalled. He had stressed that the main aim of the Australian group in Shanghai at the present time was to save Australians from the horrors of a pending war on their own soil, and to evolve an honourable peace and withdrawal from the War.

The local Australian leader had pointed out that at home, Australians were moving for a withdrawal from the conflict and that Mr. Forde, Australian War Minister, was seeking to stifle this movement. However, it was stated, he would do his utmost to win the support of all his compatriots in the Far East and to draw Australians outside the scheme of European politics.

这位本地澳洲领袖指出，在国内，澳洲人正在推动退出冲突，而澳洲战争部长福尔德（Forde）先生正试图扼杀这一运动。然而，据称，他将竭尽全力赢得远东所有同胞的支持，并将澳洲人从欧洲政治的 schemes 中拉出来。

March 13, 1942.

The meeting of the Independent Australia League was
held in camera yesterday afternoon at the Palace Hotel,
members of the press were excluded. However, the Japanese
Army is supporting the movement as Mr. Ueno of the Intelli-
gence Section of the Army was present. The first meeting
held last Saturday was attended by Sergeant-Major Furuta
attached to the Foreign Section of the Gendarmerie.

There were about a dozen local Australians at the
meeting presided over by Mr. Allen Raymond. The following
notes were secured from Mr. Ueno this morning :-

"It has been proposed to carry a three-hour daily
Australian morning program over Station XMHA and one hour
at night. It will be a program "Calling Australia" in
which messages from Australians in the Orient will be
broadcast as well as petitions urging Australians to vote
for a withdrawal from the present Pacific crisis.

"Should this program fail," Mr. Ueno stated, "it is the
intention of the Japanese authorities to contact all
Australians in occupied areas and give them a chance to go
with the Japanese to Australia and there run the adminis-
tration."

The keynote of yesterday's meeting, said Mr. Ueno,
was to point out the attitude of he British towards
Australians in the last World War and the present, where
Australians were made the cat's paw of the British. The
number of Australians sacrificed in the Libya campaign, Singapore
and N.E.I. were glaring examples.

Among those present at yesterday's meeting was Miss
MacDonald, who has been exiled from Australia, due to her
persistent urges urging that Australia be independent.
One Mr. Colman of Jardine Matheson was also present but is
known among local circles as a staunch British patriot and
his presence was a surprise. His action at present would
bear watching.

1942 年 3 月 13 日。

“独立澳大利亚联盟”的会议于昨日下午在华懋饭店闭门举行，新闻界成员被排除在外。然而，日本陆军支持该运动，因为陆军情报科的上野（Ueno）先生出席了会议。上周六举行的第一次会议有隶属于宪兵队外事科的古田（Furuta）军曹参加。

约有十几名在沪澳洲人参加了由艾伦·雷蒙德（Allen Raymond）先生主持的会议。今晨从上野先生处获得了以下笔记：-

“已提议通过 XMHA 电台每天播放三小时的澳洲晨间节目和一小时的夜间节目。这将是一个‘呼叫澳大利亚’（Calling Australia）节目，其中将广播来自东方澳洲人的讯息，以及敦促澳洲人投票退出当前太平洋危机的请愿书。

上野先生表示：‘如果该节目失败，日本当局打算接触占领区内的所有澳洲人，给他们一个随日本人前往澳大利亚并在那里管理行政的机会。’”

上野先生说，昨天会议的主旨是指出英国在上次世界大战及当前对澳洲人的态度，即澳洲人沦为英国的爪牙。在利比亚战役、新加坡和荷属东印度群岛（N.E.I.）牺牲的澳洲人数量就是明显的例子。

出席昨天会议的还有麦克唐纳（MacDonald）小姐，她因坚持敦促澳大利亚独立而被驱逐出澳大利亚。怡和洋行（Jardine Matheson）的一位科尔曼（Colman）先生也出席了会议，但他在本地圈子里以坚定的英国爱国者而闻名，他的出席令人惊讶。他目前的行动值得监视。

page_data.en:
The first "Calling Australia" program will be
broadcast to-night over Station XMHA, concluded Mr. Ueno.

Lt-Colonel Mann of the S.V.C. has been doing everything
possible to frustrate the movement. This is known to the
Japanese authorities, said Mr. Ueno.

上野先生总结道，第一个“呼叫澳大利亚”节目将于今晚通过 XMHA 电台广播。

义勇军（S.V.C.）的曼（Mann）中校一直在尽一切可能挫败该运动。上野先生说，日本当局对此知情。

Independent
Australians
Form Group

A group of independent-minded Australians met in Shanghai yesterday afternoon at the Palace Hotel and organized a "Breakaway Australia" movement, thus inaugurating the much anticipated Australian independence group that has been talked of among the local Australian community in the past few weeks.

The meeting was called to order by Mr. Allan Raymond, Australian stockbroker from Sydney. A resolution was passed during the meeting, which stipulated:

1.—The "Breakaway Australia" movement will immediately seek ways and means of promoting independence for Australia.

2.—The "Breakaway Australia" movement will strongly advocate the withdrawal of Australia from participation in World War II.

3.—Negotiations to be opened by which Australia might honourably conclude a separate peace with Japan.

It was also proposed that the movement should appeal to the Japanese authorities for clemency in the latter's prosecution of war against Australia.

会议由来自悉尼的澳洲股票经纪人艾伦·雷蒙德（Allan Raymond）先生召集。会议期间通过了一项决议，规定：

1.—“澳大利亚分离”运动将立即寻求促进澳大利亚独立的途径和方法。

2.—“澳大利亚分离”运动将强烈主张澳大利亚退出参与第二次世界大战。

3.—开启谈判，以便澳大利亚可以与日本光荣地达成单独和平。

会议还提议，该运动应向日本当局呼吁，在对澳作战中予以宽大处理。
